subject.title: [Feature]: Expose immutable inbound message context to Codex native runs for safe reply and reaction routing

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic run-bound inbound-event and current-target action contract for plugins and runtimes, with Codex native tools consuming that shared contract rather than receiving a Codex-specific environment escape hatch?
rationale: The request needs a durable security and compatibility boundary across channel adapters, agent scheduling, plugin hooks, and native runtimes; source evidence shows the existing hook surface cannot supply that behavior safely.

options.title: Design a generic current-target contract
options.body: Define authenticated run binding, typed reply/react-current actions, and event idempotency below the Codex-specific bridge, then expose it to supported runtimes.

options.title: Keep the existing hook boundary
options.body: Document that plugins must use prompt-visible metadata or their own delivery flow and do not receive verified native-tool routing transforms.

options.title: Defer until a channel-runtime proposal
options.body: Ask for a narrowed design covering queue semantics, authorization, and the plugin SDK compatibility surface before committing to new APIs.

recommendation.title: Design a generic current-target contract
recommendation.body: Define authenticated run binding, typed reply/react-current actions, and event idempotency below the Codex-specific bridge, then expose it to supported runtimes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the Codex native tool and dynamic-tool boundary makes this the closest evidence-backed routing candidate.
